title: On OPT? Check W-2 boxes 4 and 6.
label: F-1 Tax Check

hook.sub: You may have paid tax you didn't owe.

items.l: Social Security + Medicare on OPT pay

items.t: W-2s are due to you by Feb 1, 2027

captions.instagram:
On OPT? Check your W-2 before you file. 🎓

F-1 students who are still nonresidents for tax (generally under 5 calendar years in the US) are generally exempt from Social Security and Medicare tax on OPT wages.

Example: on $40,000 of OPT pay, that's $3,060 that may not have been owed.

✔️ Look at W-2 boxes 4 and 6 (W-2s are due to you by Feb 1, 2027).
✔️ Taken out anyway? Ask your employer's payroll first.
✔️ Payroll can't fix it? Form 843 + Form 8316 go to the IRS.

Comment FICA with your F-1 tax question. Tax questions only; work authorization questions go to your DSO.

Source: IRS, Foreign student liability for Social Security and Medicare taxes. General information, not advice for your situation.

captions.youtube_description: F-1, J-1 and M-1 students who are nonresident aliens for tax (generally under 5 calendar years in the US) are generally exempt from Social Security and Medicare tax on allowed wages, including OPT. Example: $40,000 of OPT pay, $3,060 of Social Security and Medicare. Check W-2 boxes 4 and 6. If it was withheld, ask your employer's payroll first; if they can't fix it, file Form 843 with Form 8316. Sources: IRS foreign student FICA page, Topic 751, W-2 instructions. Tax only; work authorization questions go to your DSO. General information, not advice for your situation.
